commitResults.messageBody:
Add reusable skills for code quality, Git conventions, coding standards
and UI testing. Update AGENTS.md to require code-quality and compliance

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertion checks for task list size after modification
Validate task types for storage format
commitResults.messageBody:
Ensure that task serialization receives a supported type so that
unexpected task types are detected.
chore(java): Add defensive assertions for task management

Propagate file creation, reading and writing issues using
AnswerMeException. Keep the configured data file in one field
so that all storage operations use the same path.

Storage#parseTask currently mixes parsing, validation and task
construction while relying on unexplained storage-format literals.
This makes the deserialization flow harder to understand.

These are the changes in this commit:
- Replace magic literals with named constants/enums
- Apply SLAP to Storage#parseTask by extracting private helper methods

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser class: reject duplicate or improperly separated flags
Parser class: Fix error message for event flags
Parser: convert magic literals to named constants
Show confirmations only after saving tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Add, delete, mark and unmark commands currently report success before the
updated task list is saved. Even if persistence fails, users still receive
confirmation messages for data that was not written to disk.

Display confirmation messages only after storage succeeds. Allow AddCommand
to propagate storage failures so the caller can report the error instead of
presenting a misleading success state.

Ui#showMessage currently mixes response tracking with console-specific
formatting. Shared values and method names also do not clearly express
their roles.

- Apply SLAP by extracting Ui#printMessageToConsole from Ui#showMessage
to make the flow of messages clearer.
- Represent shared Ui elements as constants.
- Rename Ui#printShortWelcome to Ui#getShortWelcome to better reflect
its behaviour.

Datetime parsing currently rebuilds formatters for each instance
and uses empty catch blocks to try the next format in each loop
iteration.

Update the class to adhere to SLAP and code quality principles.
- Use shared formatters with an explicit Locale and strict validation.
- Provide clearer validation error messages.
- Convert DateTimeParser#parseDateTime to static since it does not
have instance-specific state.

application.

commitResults.messageTitle: Style bot replies by response type
commitResults.messageBody:
Bot replies currently use the same appearance, making successful
commands and errors difficult to distinguish.

Propagate response types through command results and apply distinct
styles to normal, successful and error responses. This enables clear
visual feedback without relying on response wording.
- NORMAL: list, find, bye
- SUCCESS: todo, deadline, event, mark, unmark, delete, dedup
- ERROR: invalid commands and storage failures
